mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY growth > 2% does not lead to tighter monetary policy within the next 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or UNRATE decrease does not correlate with increased consumer confidence within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over 3 consecutive months signals increased demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with broader economic growth indicators within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals increased economic activity, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase does not correlate with increased economic activity within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4%, and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% YoY, it signals a restrictive monetary policy in a slowing economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening in a slowing economy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of high FEDFUNDS and low GDPC1 growth does not lead to negative equity returns.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3%, signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease does not correlate with increased consumer spending within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over 3 consecutive months signals robust consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or RSAFS increase does not correlate with broader economic growth indicators within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) decreases by more than 0.5% in a quarter, it signals a loosening monetary policy, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decrease does not lead to loosening monetary policy within the next quarter.
